claim: The bacterial Cas9 needs to be efficiently shuttled into the nucleus as attempted by fusion with nuclear localization signals (NLSs).
source: The bacterial Cas9 needs to be efficiently shuttled into the nucleus as attempted by fusion with nuclear localization signals (NLSs).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about Cas9 function and common practice in the field.

claim: Additional peptide tags such as FLAG- or myc-tags are usually added for immediate detection or straightforward purification.
source: Additional peptide tags such as FLAG- or myc-tags are usually added for immediate detection or straightforward purification.
evidence: This describes common practice in the field of protein tagging.

claim: The addition of the hei-tag to Cas9 or a C-to-T (cytosine-to-thymine) base editor dramatically enhances the respective targeting efficiency.
source: The addition of the hei-tag, a myc-tag coupled to an optimized NLS via a flexible linker, to Cas9 or a C-to-T (cytosine-to-thymine) base editor dramatically enhances the respective targeting efficiency.
evidence: This is the main finding of the study, supported by experimental data presented in multiple figures.

claim: The hei-tag boost results in an increase in bi-allelic editing.
source: This results in an increase in bi-allelic editing, yet reduction of allele variance, indicating an immediate activity even at early developmental stages.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing increased pigmentation loss in embryos.

claim: The hei-tag boost results in reduction of allele variance.
source: This results in an increase in bi-allelic editing, yet reduction of allele variance, indicating an immediate activity even at early developmental stages.
evidence: This is supported by sequencing data showing fewer distinct alleles in heiCas9 experiments.

claim: The hei-tag boost indicates an immediate activity even at early developmental stages.
source: This results in an increase in bi-allelic editing, yet reduction of allele variance, indicating an immediate activity even at early developmental stages.
evidence: This is inferred from the reduced allele variance and increased bi-allelic editing.

claim: The hei-tag boost is active in model systems ranging from fish to mammals, including tissue culture applications.
source: The hei-tag boost is active in model systems ranging from fish to mammals, including tissue culture applications.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from medaka, zebrafish, and mouse cell culture.

claim: The simple addition of the hei-tag allows to instantly upgrade existing and potentially highly adapted systems.
source: The simple addition of the hei-tag allows to instantly upgrade existing and potentially highly adapted systems as well as to establish novel highly efficient tools immediately applicable at the mRNA level.
evidence: This is supported by the demonstration that adding the hei-tag to different Cas9 variants and base editors improves their performance.

claim: In the last decade, the CRISPR/Cas9 system and its derivatives facilitated and revolutionized genome editing across all phyla.
source: In the last decade, the CRISPR/Cas9 system and its derivatives facilitated and revolutionized genome editing across all phyla (Nidhi et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: The efficiency of editing crucially depends on the on-site activity of the particular Cas9 enzymes used in the nucleus.
source: The efficiency of editing crucially depends on the on-site activity of the particular Cas9 enzymes used (usually Streptococcus pyogenes Cas9, SpCas9) in the nucleus.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the CRISPR field.

claim: State-of-the-art Cas9 variants differ by peptide tags added to the N- and C-termini of the respective endonuclease resulting in reported different activities.
source: State-of-the-art Cas9 variants differ by peptide tags added to the N- and C-termini of the respective endonuclease resulting in reported different activities (Liu et al., 2021; Zhang et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The monopartite NLS originating from the SV40 large T-antigen is routinely employed to achieve nuclear localization of the Cas9 enzyme.
source: To achieve nuclear localization of the Cas9 enzyme, the monopartite NLS originating from the SV40 large T-antigen (Kalderon et al., 1984) or a bipartite NLS discovered in Xenopus nucleoplasmin is routinely employed (Dingwall et al., 1988).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: A bipartite NLS discovered in Xenopus nucleoplasmin is routinely employed to achieve nuclear localization of the Cas9 enzyme.
source: To achieve nuclear localization of the Cas9 enzyme, the monopartite NLS originating from the SV40 large T-antigen (Kalderon et al., 1984) or a bipartite NLS discovered in Xenopus nucleoplasmin is routinely employed (Dingwall et al., 1988).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The nuclear localization activity of commonly used NLSs is tightly controlled during early development.
source: However, the nuclear localization activity of commonly used NLSs is tightly controlled during early development (Poon and Jans, 2005) and is first detectable during gastrulation.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: In fish embryos, an optimized artificial NLS (oNLS) facilitates prominent nuclear localization already immediately after fertilization.
source: In fish embryos, an optimized artificial NLS (Inoue et al., 2016) (oNLS) facilitates prominent nuclear localization already immediately after fertilization, while the SV40 NLS acts most prominently much later and facilitates nuclear localization approximately at the 1000-cell stage.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: The SV40 NLS acts most prominently much later and facilitates nuclear localization approximately at the 1000-cell stage in fish embryos.
source: In fish embryos, an optimized artificial NLS (Inoue et al., 2016) (oNLS) facilitates prominent nuclear localization already immediately after fertilization, while the SV40 NLS acts most prominently much later and facilitates nuclear localization approximately at the 1000-cell stage.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: For high targeting efficiency with low mosaicism, a peak activity should be achieved in the zygote or at early cleavage stages.
source: For high targeting efficiency with low mosaicism, a peak activity should be achieved in the zygote or at early cleavage stages.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about developmental biology and genome editing.

claim: The hei-tag is a short bipartite tag composed of a myc-tag and optimized NLSs at the N- and C-termini.
source: Here, we present the hei-tag, a short bipartite tag composed of a myc-tag and optimized NLSs at the N- and C-termini, that boosts Cas9 or cytosine-to-thymine (C-to-T) base editor-mediated targeted genome editing in organismo and cell culture.
evidence: This is a description of the construct developed in this study.

claim: The hei-tag boosts Cas9 or cytosine-to-thymine (C-to-T) base editor-mediated targeted genome editing in organismo and cell culture.
source: Here, we present the hei-tag, a short bipartite tag composed of a myc-tag and optimized NLSs at the N- and C-termini, that boosts Cas9 or cytosine-to-thymine (C-to-T) base editor-mediated targeted genome editing in organismo and cell culture.
evidence: This is the main finding supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: Only bi-allelic inactivation of oca2 results in the loss of pigmentation of eyes and skin.
source: Only its bi-allelic inactivation results in the loss of pigmentation of eyes and skin (Lischik et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Medaka and zebrafish cover a wide evolutionary distance of 200 million years.
source: We established a quantitative assay for loss-of-eye pigmentation to address the activity of different Cas9 variants in two teleost model systems, medaka (Oryzias latipes) and zebrafish (Danio rerio) covering a wide evolutionary distance of 200 million years (Furutani-Seiki and Wittbrodt, 2004).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: heiCas9 displayed a 70% increase in bi-allelic targeting efficiency vs. the reference zCas9 in medaka at high molar excess.
source: When assessing the activity of the resulting heiCas9 at high molar excess (standard conditions, 150 ng/µl), heiCas9 displayed a 70% increase in bi-allelic targeting efficiency vs. the reference zCas9 (median zCas9 = 134.5, heiCas9 = 225.3; Figure 1d) in medaka.
evidence: This is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 1d.

claim: The editing efficiency of injected heiCas9 mRNA was fully comparable to RNP approaches.
source: Strikingly, the editing efficiency of injected heiCas9 mRNA was fully comparable to such RNP approaches (Figure 1d, Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1d and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: heiCas9 delivered a 17-fold increase in targeting efficiency compared to zCas9 in zebrafish.
source: Taking the activity of zCas9 as base level (median = 14.7), heiCas9 delivered an outstanding targeting efficiency (median = 254.6), reflecting a 17-fold increase (p = 2.1e-56) (Figure 1g, Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 1g.

claim: In all multiplexing cases, heiCas9 performed dramatically better than the reference zCas9.
source: In all cases, heiCas9 performed dramatically better than the reference zCas9 (Figure 2a; mean percentage of modified alleles zCas9 [black dots] vs. heiCas9 [red dots]: OlOca2: 3.38% vs. 54.59%, p = 0.026; OlRx2: 20.82% vs. 95.85%, p = 3.2e-06; OlRx3: 16.61% vs. 49.36%, p = 0.0041; OlCryaa: 83.50% vs. 98.44%, p = 0.039).
evidence: This is supported by Illumina sequencing data shown in Figure 2a.

claim: The allele variance was reduced in all cases when using heiCas9 in multiplexing experiments.
source: Strikingly, although the overall targeting efficiency was consistently higher as reflected by the high percentage of edited alleles (Figure 2a), at the same time the allele variance was reduced in all cases when using heiCas9 (Figure 2b; mean percentage of allele variance: zCas9 [black hollow dots] vs. heiCas9 [red hollow dots]: OlOca2: 20.71% vs. 12.87%, p = 0.025; OlRx2: 15.63% vs. 7.86%, p = 7.6e-06; OlRx3: 17.91% vs. 12.75%, p = 0.00021; OlCryaa: 10.17% vs. 8.74%, p = 0.22).
evidence: This is supported by Illumina sequencing data shown in Figure 2b.

claim: heiCas9 also exhibited the highest genome editing efficiency when compared to JDS246-Cas9 and GeneArt CRISPR nuclease in mammalian cell culture.
source: Similar to targeting in organismo, heiCas9 also exhibited the highest genome editing efficiency when compared to JDS246-Cas9 (TIDE: 123.6%, ICE: 113%) and GeneArt CRISPR nuclease (TIDE: 123.1%, ICE: 111%) in mammalian cell culture (Figure 3, Figure 3—figure supplement 1, R2 > 0.9 (TIDE) and >0.9 (ICE) for all mRNAs tested).
evidence: This is supported by TIDE and ICE analysis data shown in Figure 3.

claim: The KO-score efficiencies (ICE) for heiCas9 amounted to 173% compared to JDS246-Cas9 and to 167% compared to GeneArt CRISPR nuclease in mammalian cell culture.
source: Notably, the KO-score efficiencies (ICE) amounted to 173% compared to JDS246-Cas9 and to 167% compared to GeneArt CRISPR nuclease, indicating higher abundance of frameshifts (Hsiau et al., 2018) at this genomic locus.
evidence: This is supported by ICE analysis data and a citation explaining the meaning of KO-score.

claim: For each sgRNA employed, heiBE4-Gam resulted in more pronounced loss of pigmentation in comparison to BE4-Gam.
source: For each sgRNA employed, heiBE4-Gam resulted in more pronounced loss of pigmentation in comparison to BE4-Gam (Figure 4a; control median = 0.0; medians BE4-Gam vs. heiBE4-Gam: OlOca2 T1, 0.6 vs. 28.0, p = 1.737e-20; OlOca2 T3, 0.0 vs. 0.8, p = 0.0471; OlOca2 T4, 93.8 vs. 170.1, p = 5.215e-12).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative pigmentation data shown in Figure 4a.

claim: Quantification of Sanger sequencing reads confirmed an increase of all C-to-T transitions at the OlOca2 T1 target site when heiBE4-Gam was used.
source: Quantification of Sanger sequencing reads confirmed an increase of all C-to-T transitions at the OlOca2 T1 target site when heiBE4-Gam was used (74.1% ± 8.9% for heiBE4-Gam vs. 44.2% ± 6.8% for BE4-Gam; Figure 4—figure supplement 1, three replicates containing five randomly picked embryos each).
evidence: This is supported by Sanger sequencing data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The C997T transition introducing a pre-mature STOP codon was increased 1.7-fold in case of heiBE4-Gam.
source: In particular, the C997T transition introducing a pre-mature STOP codon was increased 1.7-fold (i.e. 68% in heiBE4-Gam vs. 41% in BE4-Gam) in case of heiBE4-Gam (Figure 4b and c).
evidence: This is supported by Sanger sequencing data shown in Figure 4b and c.

claim: Using the hei-tag to extend the ORFs of a mammalian codon-optimized SpCas9 or a C-to-T base editor (BE4-Gam) severely enhanced the respective genome targeting efficiency.
source: In conclusion, using the hei-tag to extend the ORFs of a mammalian codon-optimized SpCas9 or a C-to-T base editor (BE4-Gam) severely enhanced the respective genome targeting efficiency.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion supported by all the experimental data presented.

claim: The use of the optimized NLS in the hei-tag explains the earlier and better performance of the hei-tagged versions of Cas9 and base editors in developing organisms.
source: While the use of the optimized NLS in the hei-tag explains the earlier and better performance of the hei-tagged versions of Cas9 and base editors in developing organisms, the impact of the specific topology of domains contained in the hei-tag remains elusive.
evidence: This is an inference based on the known function of the optimized NLS and the experimental results.

claim: The impact of the specific topology of domains contained in the hei-tag remains elusive.
source: While the use of the optimized NLS in the hei-tag explains the earlier and better performance of the hei-tagged versions of Cas9 and base editors in developing organisms, the impact of the specific topology of domains contained in the hei-tag remains elusive.
evidence: This acknowledges a limitation in understanding the mechanism.

claim: It is speculated that the addition of certain peptide tags influences the efficacy and specificity of the fused protein of interest, due to their different isoelectric points and charge distributions.
source: It is speculated that the addition of certain peptide tags influences the efficacy and specificity of the fused protein of interest, due to their different isoelectric points and charge distributions (Zhang et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a speculation supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: The permutation screen demonstrated that although comprising the exact same peptides, position of the particular tags relative to each other conveyed different genome editing efficiencies.
source: Interestingly, our permutation screen demonstrated that although comprising the exact same peptides (for instance, compare MFO-Cas9-O [heiCas9] vs. OMF-Cas9-O and MSF-Cas9-S vs. SMF-Cas9-S in Figure 1—figure supplement 1), position of the particular tags relative to each other conveyed different genome editing efficiencies.
evidence: This is supported by data from the permutation screen shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: heiCas9 leads to a high abundance of identical mutant alleles, important for testing specific hypotheses or introducing site-specific modifications by homology-directed repair.
source: In those systems, heiCas9 leads to a high abundance of identical mutant alleles, important for testing specific hypotheses or introducing site-specific modifications by homology-directed repair (Gutierrez-Triana et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by the experimental data showing reduced allele variance and a citation to a relevant method.

claim: Cas9 variants without the hei-tag are better suited for targeted screening approaches since they introduce a large number of different mutant alleles.
source: Conversely, Cas9 variants without the hei-tag are better suited for targeted screening approaches since they introduce a large number of different mutant alleles.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that non-hei-tagged Cas9 produces higher allele variance.

claim: heiCas9 markedly increased the (bi-allelic) targeting rate alongside a decrease in allele variance, indicating a high targeting efficiency already at the earliest stages of development.
source: heiCas9 markedly increased the (bi-allelic) targeting rate alongside a decrease in allele variance, indicating a high targeting efficiency already at the earliest stages of development.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: Early targeting in developing organisms was most of all reported using RNPs.
source: Precedentially such early targeting in developing organisms was most of all reported using RNPs (Kroll et al., 2021; Wu et al., 2018), yet mRNA injection of heiCas9 is fully comparable to these protein approaches.
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: mRNA injection of heiCas9 is fully comparable to RNP protein approaches.
source: Precedentially such early targeting in developing organisms was most of all reported using RNPs (Kroll et al., 2021; Wu et al., 2018), yet mRNA injection of heiCas9 is fully comparable to these protein approaches.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data comparing heiCas9 mRNA to RNP injections.

claim: New Cas9 variants can easily be generated and produced cost-efficiently by highly reproducible in vitro transcription, a standard method in molecular biology labs.
source: The benefits of using mRNA over protein are apparent: new Cas9 variants can easily be generated and produced cost-efficiently by highly reproducible in vitro transcription, a standard method in molecular biology labs.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about molecular biology methods.

claim: The addition of the hei-tag provides the means to boost current specialized and future variants.
source: In light of the ever-expanding CRISPR tool kit, the addition of the hei-tag provides the means to boost current specialized and future variants, as the simple addition of the hei-tag sequence also potentiated the activity of a cytosine base editor, with heiBE4-Gam resulting in an overall increase of about 30% of C-to-T transition rates (Figure 4 and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing improved base editor performance.

claim: heiBE4-Gam resulted in an overall increase of about 30% of C-to-T transition rates.
source: In light of the ever-expanding CRISPR tool kit, the addition of the hei-tag provides the means to boost current specialized and future variants, as the simple addition of the hei-tag sequence also potentiated the activity of a cytosine base editor, with heiBE4-Gam resulting in an overall increase of about 30% of C-to-T transition rates (Figure 4 and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by Sanger sequencing data shown in Figure 4 and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The boosting activity of the hei-tag is neither limited by the species nor the approach.
source: Taken together, the boosting activity of the hei-tag is neither limited by the species nor the approach, making it a powerful tweak to swiftly upgrade any specifically adapted Cas-based genome editing approach (Anzalone et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from multiple species and applications, plus a citation.

claim: The hei-tag makes it a powerful tweak to swiftly upgrade any specifically adapted Cas-based genome editing approach.
source: Taken together, the boosting activity of the hei-tag is neither limited by the species nor the approach, making it a powerful tweak to swiftly upgrade any specifically adapted Cas-based genome editing approach (Anzalone et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data and supported by a citation.

claim: Base editing is an increasingly applied method with a potential for therapeutics.
source: Base editing is an increasingly applied method with a potential for therapeutics (Antoniou et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Base editors are composed of a modified Cas9 that only nicks one DNA strand and does not introduce a double-strand break (Cas9 nickase or Cas9n) and a nucleotide deaminase for precisely targeted nucleotide editing.
source: Base editors are composed of a modified Cas9 that only nicks one DNA strand and does not introduce a double-strand break (Cas9 nickase or Cas9n) and a nucleotide deaminase for precisely targeted nucleotide editing (Anzalone et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: To increase the efficiency of base editors, several iterative rounds of optimization of the employed deaminases and linkers have been undertaken, yielding optimal performance with the newest variants.
source: To increase the efficiency of base editors, several iterative rounds of optimization of the employed deaminases and linkers have been undertaken, yielding optimal performance with the newest variants (Carrington et al., 2020; Cornean et al., 2022; Rosello et al., 2021; Zhao et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Medaka embryos were fixed at 4.5 days post fertilization (dpf) well after the onset of pigmentation in control injections.
source: Injected embryos were fixed at 4.5 days post fertilization (dpf) (Iwamatsu, 2004) well after the onset of pigmentation in control injections and subjected to image analysis (Figure 1b).
evidence: This describes the experimental protocol with a citation for the developmental stage.

claim: The analysis of medaka oca2 knock-out embryos injected with zCas9 revealed bi-allelic inactivation events of the oca2 gene, yet with a strong overall variability as apparent by patchy unpigmented domains in the eyes.
source: The analysis of medaka oca2 knock-out embryos injected with zCas9 revealed bi-allelic inactivation events of the oca2 gene, yet with a strong overall variability as apparent by patchy unpigmented domains in the eyes (median of mean gray values = 134.5 compared to uninjected controls, median = 0.4; Figure 1d).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 1d.

claim: The patchy distribution of small, unpigmented areas indicated that bi-allelic targeting occurred only in few cells at later stages of development.
source: This patchy distribution of small, unpigmented areas indicated that bi-allelic targeting occurred only in few cells at later stages of development.
evidence: This is an inference from the observed phenotype.

claim: The 'hei-tag' comprises a myc-tag connected via a flexible linker to an oNLS at the N-terminus complemented by a second oNLS fused to the C-terminus of a mammalian codon-optimized Cas9.
source: The hei-tag comprises a myc-tag connected via a flexible linker to an oNLS at the N-terminus complemented by a second oNLS fused to the C-terminus of a mammalian codon-optimized Cas9 (see Supplementary file 1 for sequence) and in this conformation displayed highest editing activity.
evidence: This describes the structure of the hei-tag construct.

claim: Any alteration of those domains in relative order or sequence negatively impacted on editing efficiency compared to the hei-tag.
source: Any alteration of those domains in relative order or sequence negatively impacted on editing efficiency compared to the hei-tag (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is supported by data from the permutation screen.

claim: Embryos co-injected with heiCas9 mRNA and sgRNAs against oca2 essentially lost pigmentation.
source: Embryos co-injected with heiCas9 mRNA and sgRNAs against oca2 essentially lost pigmentation.
evidence: This is supported by the quantitative pigmentation data.

claim: The observed absence of pigmentation argues for an early time point of action due to high activity and efficient nuclear translocation of the tagged heiCas9 variant already at the earliest cleavage stages.
source: The observed absence of pigmentation argues for an early time point of action due to high activity and efficient nuclear translocation of the tagged heiCas9 variant already at the earliest cleavage stages.
evidence: This is an inference from the observed phenotype and reduced allele variance.

claim: In developing organisms, the time point of genome editing essentially impacts on the allele variance, that is, the number of alleles established by the targeting attempt.
source: In developing organisms, the time point of genome editing essentially impacts on the allele variance, that is, the number of alleles established by the targeting attempt.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about developmental biology and genome editing.

claim: To immediately provide a functional editing machinery, preassembled ribonucleoproteins (RNPs) containing Cas9 protein and guide RNA are popular, employing high molar excess/high concentrations of Cas9.
source: To immediately provide a functional editing machinery, preassembled ribonucleoproteins (RNPs) containing Cas9 protein and guide RNA are popular, employing high molar excess/high concentrations of Cas9 (Kroll et al., 2021; Wu et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Nearly unpigmented embryos were obtained with the heiCas9 in zebrafish, arguing for highly efficient, early targeting.
source: Similar to the results in medaka, yet even more pronounced, nearly unpigmented embryos were obtained with the heiCas9, arguing for highly efficient, early targeting.
evidence: This is an inference from the observed phenotype.

claim: Addition of the hei-tag to a mammalian codon-optimized Cas9 resulted in the highly efficient heiCas9, which boosted the targeting efficiency 17-fold, even when used at saturating concentrations.
source: Taken together, addition of the hei-tag to a mammalian codon-optimized Cas9 resulted in the highly efficient heiCas9, which boosted the targeting efficiency 17-fold, even when used at saturating concentrations.
evidence: This is supported by the experimental data from zebrafish.

claim: heiCas9 prominently inactivated both alleles of the targeted oca2 locus, with a putatively early onset of action upon injection of heiCas9 mRNA and the respective sgRNAs at the one-cell stage.
source: It prominently inactivated both alleles of the targeted oca2 locus, with a putatively early onset of action upon injection of heiCas9 mRNA and the respective sgRNAs at the one-cell stage.
evidence: This is supported by the experimental data showing high bi-allelic editing and reduced allele variance.

claim: In the multiplexing approaches, a total of 823,898 reads for the zCas9 and 824,817 reads for the heiCas9, compared to 711,739 control reads, were analyzed.
source: In the multiplexing approaches, a total of 823,898 reads for the zCas9 and 824,817 reads for the heiCas9, compared to 711,739 control reads, were analyzed (Supplementary file 3, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes the amount of sequencing data analyzed.

claim: The reduced allele variance for all multiplexed loci indicates an early editing by heiCas9.
source: This reduced allele variance for all multiplexed loci indicates an early editing by heiCas9.
evidence: This is an inference from the observed reduction in allele variance.

claim: The high efficiency of heiCas9 allows efficient editing at low concentrations with the potential to reduce off-target effects.
source: The high efficiency of heiCas9 thus allows efficient editing at low concentrations with the potential to reduce off-target effects.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the observed high efficiency at low concentrations.

claim: Whether the putative reduction of off-targets is (over-)compensated by the efficient nuclear localization needs to be assessed by whole-genome sequencing approaches in the future.
source: Whether this putative reduction of off-targets is (over-)compensated by the efficient nuclear localization needs to be assessed by whole-genome sequencing approaches in the future.
evidence: This acknowledges a limitation and suggests future work.

claim: heiCas9-transfected cells showed a highly increased number of mutant alleles with an increased abundance of a 26 nt deletion when compared to GeneArt CRISPR nuclease and JDS246-Cas9.
source: Remarkably, heiCas9-transfected cells showed a highly increased number of mutant alleles with an increased abundance of a 26 nt deletion when compared to GeneArt CRISPR nuclease and JDS246-Cas9 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The transition of cytosines 766, 922, and 997 to thymine all convert the respective codon to a pre-mature STOP in the oca2 ORF.
source: In the oca2 ORF, the transition of cytosines 766, 922, and 997 to thymine all convert the respective codon to a pre-mature STOP (OlOca2 T3: C766T, leading to Q256*; OlOca2 T4: C922T, leading to Q308*; OlOca2 T1: C995-997T, leading to T332I and Q333*).
evidence: This describes the expected outcome of base editing at specific positions.

claim: All experimental procedures were performed according to the guidelines of the German animal welfare law and approved by the local government.
source: All experimental procedures were performed according to the guidelines of the German animal welfare law and approved by the local government (Tierschutzgesetz §11, Abs. 1, Nr. 1, husbandry permit number 35-9185.64/BH Wittbrodt).
evidence: This is a statement about ethical compliance.

claim: Mouse SW10 cells were regularly tested negative for mycoplasma infections.
source: Mouse SW10 cells (ATCC, CRL-2766, Lot number 4117643) were cultured in DMEM (Gibco) supplemented with 1 g/ml glucose containing 10% FCS (Sigma), 1% penicillin (10,000 units/ml; Gibco), and 1% streptomycin (10 mg/ml; Gibco) and maintained at 33°C and 5% CO2 and regularly tested negative for mycoplasma infections.
evidence: This describes quality control of the cell line used.
